text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- In Parliament, Prime Minister Gyula Horn pledged a relentless investigation into the top-level management of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. @

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and visiting Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin discussed a project whereby some 1.4 billion cubic metres of natural gas will be shipped from Kazakhstan to Hungary in exchange for work carried out by Hungarian labourers at Tengiz over recent years.
- Portuguese Defence Minister Antonio Vitorino signed a bilateral military cooperation framework agreement in Budapest.
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told a meeting of the economic cabinet that he sees no opportunity for a further pension increase this year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs warned in Parliament that remarks made by certain party leaders concerning border revisions could jeopardize Hungary's efforts at European integration.
- General Klaus Naumann, chairman of the NATO military commission, arrived in Budapest Monday evening for an introductory visit.
- The Procurement Managers' Index in September was 60.4 percent, showing an upswing in the domestic economy in September compared to August. @
- The central bank will issue new HUF 100 coins as of October 21 this year.
- Police seized nearly 2,000 tablets of Extasy of HUF 4.7 million street value in a routine traffic check on a Skoda car in Tiszaujvaros.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Hungary's admission to the International Energy Agency is expected to be confirmed at next Wednesday's session of the board of management of thw OECD's energy agency. @

- The scale of planned energy price increases in January will be discussed today at a meeting with the participation of the Hungarian Energy Office, power plants, electricity and gas suppliers, and will be announced late October.
- "The Sony Corporation is considering further investments in Hungary," managing director of the multinational company Kei Kodera has told this paper.
- The shopping centre chain Centrum began a week-long project on Monday named the "Week of Hungarian Products".
NAPI GAZDASAG @

- In a country-by-country risk list related to creditworthiness published by the New York periodical Institutional Investor in September, Hungary received 44.7 points, 1.1 points higher than in March, placing it in 50th place on the list.

- Nearly 1,400 food shops went out of business in the first half of this year, most of them small retail outlets, while international discount food stores are expected to expand, Amer Nielsen Research has reported.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
